front: C'est le plus beau jour de ma vie.
pronunciation: [seh luh plü boh zhoor duh mah VEE]
back: It's the best day of my life.
context: Superlative: le/la/les + plus/moins + adjective. 'De' (not 'dans') introduces the group: de ma vie.

front: C'est la ville la plus touristique de France.
pronunciation: [seh lah veel lah plü too-rees-TEEK duh FRAHNS]
back: It's the most touristy city in France.
context: When the adjective follows the noun, repeat the article: la ville LA plus touristique.

front: C'est le plat le moins cher du menu.
pronunciation: [seh luh plah luh mwan SHEHR dü muh-NÜ]
back: It's the cheapest dish on the menu.
context: 'Le moins' = the least.

front: C'est le meilleur restaurant du quartier.
pronunciation: [seh luh meh-yuhr res-toh-RAHN dü kar-TYAY]
back: It's the best restaurant in the neighborhood.
context: Bon → le meilleur (never 'le plus bon').

front: C'est elle qui chante le mieux.
pronunciation: [seh tel kee shahnt luh MYUH]
back: She's the one who sings best.
context: Bien → le mieux (adverb, invariable).

front: C'est le pire film que j'aie jamais vu.
pronunciation: [seh luh peer feelm kuh zhay zhah-meh VÜ]
back: It's the worst film I've ever seen.
context: After a superlative + que, French uses the subjunctive: 'que j'aie jamais vu'.

front: C'est la plus belle chose qui me soit arrivée.
pronunciation: [seh lah plü bel shohz kee muh swah tah-ree-VAY]
back: It's the most beautiful thing that's ever happened to me.
context: Superlative + qui + subjunctive (soit arrivée).

front: Le mont Blanc est le plus haut sommet d'Europe occidentale.
pronunciation: [luh mohn BLAHN eh luh plü oh soh-meh duh-rop ok-see-dahn-TAL]
back: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in Western Europe.
context: About 4,800 m high, on the French-Italian border.

front: La Loire est le plus long fleuve de France.
pronunciation: [lah LWAHR eh luh plü lohn fluhv duh FRAHNS]
back: The Loire is the longest river in France.
context: 'Un fleuve' flows into the sea; 'une rivière' into another river.

front: C'est lui qui travaille le plus.
pronunciation: [seh lwee kee trah-vahy luh PLÜS]
back: He's the one who works the most.
context: With verbs: verb + le plus / le moins.

front: C'est elle qui a le plus d'expérience.
pronunciation: [seh tel kee ah luh plü dek-spay-RYAHNS]
back: She's the one with the most experience.
context: With nouns: le plus de / le moins de + noun.

front: C'est l'une des plus grandes villes du monde.
pronunciation: [seh lün day plü grahnd veel dü MOHND]
back: It's one of the biggest cities in the world.
context: 'L'un(e) des' + plural superlative = one of the…

front: C'était vraiment super !
pronunciation: [seh-teh vreh-mahn sü-PEHR]
back: It was really great!
context: Intensifiers: vraiment, très, super, hyper (informal).

front: Ce gâteau est extrêmement bon.
pronunciation: [suh gah-toh eh tek-strem-mahn BOHN]
back: This cake is extremely good.
context: 'Extrêmement' = extremely.

front: Il fait une chaleur incroyable.
pronunciation: [eel feh tün shah-luhr an-krwah-YAH-bluh]
back: It's incredibly hot.
context: 'Incroyable' = incredible.

front: Ce paysage est absolument magnifique.
pronunciation: [suh pay-ee-ZAHZH eh tab-soh-lü-mahn mah-nyee-FEEK]
back: This landscape is absolutely magnificent.
context: 'Absolument' with strong adjectives (magnifique, génial, horrible) instead of 'très'.

front: Le film était hyper long.
pronunciation: [luh feelm ay-teh ee-pehr LOHN]
back: The film was super long.
context: 'Hyper' / 'super' / 'trop' = very (informal).

front: C'est le moindre de mes soucis.
pronunciation: [seh luh mwan-druh duh may soo-SEE]
back: It's the least of my worries.
context: 'Le moindre' = the least (formal), mainly in fixed expressions.

front: Je n'ai pas la moindre idée.
pronunciation: [zhuh neh pah lah mwan-dree-DAY]
back: I haven't the slightest idea.
context: 'La moindre' = the slightest.

front: C'est vraiment le comble !
pronunciation: [seh vreh-mahn luh KOHM-bluh]
back: That's the last straw!
context: 'Le comble' = the height of something, the limit.

front: Il fait un froid glacial ce matin.
pronunciation: [eel feh tan frwah glah-SYAL suh mah-TAN]
back: It's freezing cold this morning.
context: Extreme adjectives: glacial (freezing), brûlant (scorching), énorme (huge), minuscule (tiny).

front: Leur maison est immense.
pronunciation: [luhr meh-zohn eh tee-MAHNS]
back: Their house is huge.
context: 'Immense' already means very big: no 'très' needed.

front: C'était nul, mais vraiment nul !
pronunciation: [seh-teh NÜL, meh vreh-mahn NÜL]
back: It was rubbish, really rubbish!
context: Repetition for emphasis is common in speech.

front: Je suis mort de fatigue.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee mor duh fah-TEEG]
back: I'm dead tired.
context: 'Mort de' + noun: mort de peur, mort de rire.

front: C'est la première fois que je viens ici.
pronunciation: [seh lah pruh-myehr fwah kuh zhuh vyan zee-SEE]
back: It's the first time I've come here.
context: French uses the present after 'c'est la première fois que' (English uses the present perfect).

front: C'est le seul qui m'ait aidé.
pronunciation: [seh luh SUHL kee meh teh-DAY]
back: He's the only one who helped me.
context: After 'le seul' + qui, the subjunctive is common (m'ait aidé).

front: De toutes les saisons, je préfère l'automne.
pronunciation: [duh toot lay seh-ZOHN, zhuh pray-fehr loh-TUN]
back: Of all the seasons, I prefer autumn.
context: 'De tous / de toutes' = of all.

front: C'est la moindre des choses.
pronunciation: [seh lah mwan-druh day SHOHZ]
back: It's the least I could do.
context: Reply to thanks: it was nothing.

front: Ce sont les gens les plus gentils que je connaisse.
pronunciation: [suh sohn lay zhahn lay plü zhahn-TEE kuh zhuh koh-NES]
back: They're the kindest people I know.
context: Superlative + que + subjunctive: que je connaisse.

front: Rien n'est plus important que la santé.
pronunciation: [ryan neh plü zan-por-TAHN kuh lah sahn-TAY]
back: Nothing is more important than health.
context: 'Rien n'est plus… que' = nothing is more… than.

front: Ça m'a fait le plus grand bien.
pronunciation: [sah mah feh luh plü grahn BYAN]
back: It did me a world of good.
context: 'Faire du bien' = to do good; 'le plus grand bien' = the greatest good.

front: Elle a eu la meilleure note de la classe.
pronunciation: [el ah ü lah meh-yuhr NOT duh lah KLAS]
back: She got the best grade in the class.
context: 'Meilleur' agrees: la meilleure.

front: C'est de loin le meilleur livre de l'année.
pronunciation: [seh duh LWAN luh meh-yuhr LEE-vruh duh lah-NAY]
back: It's by far the best book of the year.
context: 'De loin' = by far.

front: On a vécu les pires moments ensemble.
pronunciation: [ohn nah vay-kü lay peer moh-MAHN ahn-SAHM-bluh]
back: We went through the worst times together.
context: 'Les pires' = the worst (plural).

front: Le plus important, c'est d'être heureux.
pronunciation: [luh plü zan-por-TAHN, seh deh-truh uh-RUH]
back: The most important thing is to be happy.
context: 'Le plus important, c'est de' + infinitive.
